layer5_probe.description: Fixed diagnostic logistic probe trained on mean-pooled Layer-5 DNABERT-2 representations.
layer5_probe.interpretation: Probe scores measure promoter-associated evidence under the diagnostic readout; they are not native DNABERT-2 predictions.

layer1_mlp_direction.construction: Difference between mean promoter and non-promoter pooled Layer-1 MLP outputs.
layer1_mlp_direction.cross_validation: Five-fold stratified cross-validation; each source and all of its intervention variants were evaluated using a direction learned without that source.

main_supported_claim: Controlled GC-increasing substitutions move Layer-1 MLP activations toward a held-out promoter-associated direction, while GC-decreasing substitutions move activations away from that direction. Effects exceed mutation-count-matched GC-neutral controls and increase with intervention magnitude.
limitations: The model is a pretrained DNABERT-2 backbone with a diagnostic probe, not a fine-tuned native promoter classifier.
Base substitutions alter local sequence context, motifs, dinucleotides, and BPE tokenization in addition to GC content.
GC-neutral controls match mutation count but not the exact mutated positions or source-base classes of every directional intervention.
The results establish effects on internal representations and the downstream probe, but do not establish that the Layer-1 MLP fully mediates the downstream effect.
The source cohort contains selected recognized promoters and sampled non-promoters, limiting population-level generalization.
